title: Comparing Quantities to 10: More, Fewer and the Same
seo_title: Kindergarten Comparing quantities to 10 Worksheets: Free Math with Pictures and Answers (BC Curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Kindergarten math worksheets on comparing quantities to 10 for the BC curriculum: match one to one, more, fewer, the same, most and fewest, how many more, and bigger and smaller numbers. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_big: Match one to one: the group with some left over has more.
key_sub: If nothing is left over, the groups are the same. A longer row does not always have more.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Line up two groups and match them one to one. The group with some left over has more.
  • The other group has fewer. If nothing is left over, they are the same.
  • When we count, a bigger number comes later: 7 is more than 4.

Examples

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Thinking the longer row has moreMatch one to one, or count both rows.
Mixing up more and fewerMore means the group with extra. Fewer means not as many.
Giving the bigger number for how many moreCount only the ones left over after matching.

faq.q: How do Kindergarten children compare quantities?
faq.a: They line up two groups and match them one to one, or count both groups and compare the numbers up to 10.

faq.q: What is the difference between more and fewer?
faq.a: More is the group with extra left over after matching. Fewer is the group that runs out first.
Spreading things out can make a row look longer. Matching shows which group really has more.

faq.q: How can I practise at home?
faq.a: Put out two small piles of toys, line them up side by side, and ask which pile has more and how many more.
